items.title: 貶值壓力難解 日央行9月升息機率飆至57% 多數經濟學家押注利率升至1.25%
items.title_en: Depreciation Pressure Remains Unresolved, BOJ's September Rate Hike Odds Surge to 57% as Most Economists Bet on 1.25% Rate
paras: 日本銀行(BOJ)升息步伐可能明顯加快。路透最新調查顯示，多數經濟學家預期，日本央行最快將在9月再度升息，將目前1%的政策利率調升至1.25%，市場對最終利率的預期也同步上修。推動政策轉向的因素包括中東戰事推升進口能源成本、日元持續承壓，以及日本國內通膨壓力升高，使日本央行面臨更強烈的提前收緊貨幣政策壓力。
路透於8月17日至24日進行的調查顯示，57%的受訪經濟學家預期日本央行將在9月升息，與7月調查時僅5%的受訪者預期本季採取行動相比出現明顯逆轉。58名回答利率時點問題的受訪者中，有10人預期日本央行將在10月或12月進一步升息，將政策利率提高至1.5%。
日本央行6月已將政策利率調升至1%，創約30年來新高。市場目前關注焦點已從日本央行是否繼續升息，轉向升息速度以及本輪緊縮週期的最終利率水準。
摩根大通證券首席日本經濟學家藤田綾子(Ayako Fujita)表示，市場已在很大程度上消化日本央行9月升息的預期，如果央行此時延後行動，反而可能造成市場不穩定，因此提早調整政策已變得難以避免。
市場對日本央行中長期緊縮幅度的預期也顯著提高。54名受訪分析師中，有35人、約三分之二預期，到2027年3月底前政策利率至少將升至1.5%，比7月調查預期的時間提前約3個月。另有約60%的受訪者預期，到2027年第3季底前，日本政策利率至少將達到1.75%。
對最終利率的預期同樣大幅上修。在回答額外問題的36名受訪者中，50%認為1.75%將成為本輪緊縮週期的最終利率，高於7月時的19%；預期最終利率將達2%或更高的比例，也從7月的23%升至36%，顯示市場對日本央行政策正常化的預期正快速升溫。
日本央行近期政策討論也顯示，決策官員對加快升息步伐的支持正在擴大。部分官員認為，隨著通膨持續高於央行2%的目標，日本央行需要進一步撤回貨幣寬鬆措施；也有官員主張避免承諾固定升息節奏，但應向市場展現防止物價持續偏離目標的決心。
最新通膨數據進一步強化升息理由。日本7月核心消費者物價指數(CPI)年增1.8%，高於6月的1.6%，主要受到進口成本及能源價格變化影響。排除生鮮食品與能源後的核心通膨率也由1.7%升至1.9%，服務業通膨則持續受到薪資成長支撐，顯示日本物價壓力並未完全消退。
中東局勢成為日本貨幣政策的新變數。美國與以色列對伊朗的軍事行動及後續衝突推升油價，對高度依賴能源進口的日本形成更直接的通膨壓力。日本央行擔心，如果能源與進口成本持續攀升，加上日元維持疲弱，可能進一步推高物價預期，迫使央行加快收緊政策。
日元持續走弱也是日本央行面臨的另一項壓力。日本與美國上月罕見聯手干預匯市，在日元跌至40年低點附近後進場買進日元，以遏制日元與日本公債同步遭拋售所可能引發的外溢風險。
不過，最新調查顯示，市場對單靠匯市干預扭轉日元弱勢並不樂觀。在26名回答相關問題的經濟學家中，有18人、超過三分之二認為干預效果「不太有效」或「完全無效」，不少人認為相關行動只是延後問題爆發，並未解決日元貶值的根本因素。
美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期的發言也進一步強化9月升息預期。路透先前報導，日本央行正考慮最快9月升息，並評估在之後以比目前約每年兩次更快的速度推進緊縮政策。貝森特對日元與日本貨幣政策的關注，也被市場視為增加日本央行提前行動壓力的因素之一。
另一方面，日本首相高市早苗的財政政策可能與日本央行的抗通膨努力形成拉鋸。調查中28名回答相關問題的經濟學家裡，有25人、占89%認為，高市政府的財政政策將加劇日元走弱。
市場擔心，如果政府推動食品減稅與擴大投資支出，卻無法提出明確財源，可能進一步加重日本財政疑慮，導致日元與日本公債面臨新的拋售壓力。
野村證券首席經濟學家森田京平(Kyohei Morita)指出，高市政府的財政政策可能推高通膨預期，也加深市場對日本央行在控制物價上落後於情勢的疑慮。他警告，如果在市場已擔心缺乏財源支持的情況下進一步削減消費稅，海外投資人拋售日本公債可能加速日元貶值。
日本企業近期也開始為長期日元弱勢做準備。日元過去數年大幅貶值，導致進口能源、原物料及其他商品成本增加，企業正增加使用遠期、期貨與選擇權等工具避險。市場普遍認為，如果日本央行未能有效縮小與海外主要市場的利差或穩定通膨，日元仍可能長期維持弱勢。
日本公債市場也增加日本央行決策的複雜性。隨著殖利率上升，日本國債重新吸引部分海外資金，但更高的利率同時增加日本政府融資成本。日本央行若9月升息，可能有助於穩定日元，卻也可能進一步推升政府與企業融資成本，考驗日本龐大債務負擔及債市穩定。
整體而言，最新調查顯示，市場對日本央行政策路徑的預期已從「是否繼續升息」，轉向「升息速度會有多快、最終利率會有多高」。在日元弱勢、進口通膨、中東能源衝擊與財政擴張疑慮交織下，日本央行9月會議可能成為決定新一輪政策緊縮節奏的重要轉折點。若央行如市場預期升息至1.25%，將是日本利率正常化進程的進一步加速，也可能為2027年前後利率升向1.5%甚至1.75%以上鋪路。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) may accelerate its rate‑hike pace markedly. Reuters' latest survey shows most economists expect the BOJ to raise rates again as early as September, lifting the current 1% policy rate to 1.25%, and market expectations for the final rate have been revised upward accordingly. Drivers of a policy shift include higher imported energy costs from the Middle‑East conflict, continued yen weakness, and rising domestic inflation pressure, all putting stronger pre‑emptive tightening pressure on the BOJ.

Reuters’ survey conducted from Aug. 17‑24 found 57% of respondents expect a September hike, a sharp reversal from July when only 5% anticipated action this quarter. Of the 58 economists who answered the timing question, 10 foresee a further hike in Oct. or Dec., taking the policy rate to 1.5%.

The BOJ lifted its policy rate to 1% in June, a near‑30‑year high. Market focus has shifted from whether the BOJ will keep raising rates to how fast it will do so and what the final level of this tightening cycle will be.

Ayako Fujita, chief Japan economist at JPMorgan Securities, said the market has largely priced in a September hike; a delay now could destabilise markets, making an early policy adjustment hard to avoid.

Long‑term tightening expectations have also risen sharply. Among 54 surveyed analysts, 35 – about two‑thirds – expect the policy rate to be at least 1.5% by the end of March 2027, roughly three months earlier than July’s forecast. Around 60% anticipate the rate will reach at least 1.75% by the end of Q3 2027.

Final‑rate expectations have been revised upward as well. Of 36 respondents to a follow‑up question, 50% now see 1.75% as the ultimate rate for this cycle, up from 19% in July; the share expecting a final rate of 2% or higher rose from 23% to 36%, indicating a rapid warming of market expectations for BOJ normalisation.

Recent BOJ policy discussions show growing support among decision‑makers for a faster hike pace. Some officials argue that with inflation persistently above the 2% target, the BOJ must further unwind monetary easing; others caution against committing to a fixed hike rhythm but say the bank should demonstrate resolve to keep prices on target.

The latest inflation data further bolster the case for hikes. Japan’s core CPI rose 1.8% year‑on‑year in July, up from 1.6% in June, driven mainly by import costs and energy price changes. Core‑core inflation (excluding fresh food and energy) climbed from 1.7% to 1.9%, and services inflation remains supported by wage growth, showing price pressure has not fully abated.

Middle‑East tensions have become a new variable for Japanese monetary policy. U.S. and Israeli military actions against Iran and ensuing conflict have pushed oil prices higher, creating a more direct inflationary shock for Japan, which relies heavily on energy imports. The BOJ worries that sustained rises in energy and import costs, combined with a weak yen, could lift inflation expectations and force a faster tightening.

A persistently weak yen is another pressure on the BOJ. Japan and the United States jointly intervened in the FX market last month after the yen slipped toward a 40‑year low, buying yen to curb simultaneous selling of the yen and Japanese government bonds and avert spill‑over risks.

However, the latest survey shows scepticism about the effectiveness of FX intervention alone. Among 26 economists who answered the related question, 18 – more than two‑thirds – consider intervention “not very effective” or “completely ineffective,” with many saying such actions merely postpone the problem rather than address the root cause of yen depreciation.

Recent comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have further reinforced September‑hike expectations. Reuters previously reported that the BOJ is weighing a September hike and may accelerate tightening to a pace faster than the current roughly twice‑a‑year cadence. Bessent’s focus on the yen and Japanese policy is seen as adding pressure for the BOJ to act early.

On the fiscal side, Prime Minister Kishida’s policies could clash with the BOJ’s anti‑inflation effort. Of the 28 economists surveyed on this issue, 25 (89%) believe the Kishida administration’s fiscal stance will exacerbate yen weakness.

Markets fear that if the government pushes food tax cuts and expands investment spending without clear financing, fiscal concerns could deepen, prompting fresh selling pressure on the yen and Japanese government bonds.

Nomura chief economist Kyohei Morita warned that Kishida’s fiscal plan could raise inflation expectations and deepen doubts about the BOJ’s ability to control prices. He cautioned that further consumption‑tax cuts amid concerns over funding could trigger overseas investors to dump Japanese bonds, accelerating yen depreciation.

Japanese firms are already preparing for a prolonged yen weakness. The yen’s sharp depreciation over recent years has raised import costs for energy, raw materials and other goods, prompting companies to increase hedging with forwards, futures and options. The market broadly believes that if the BOJ cannot narrow the yield gap with overseas markets or tame inflation, the yen may stay weak for the long term.

The Japanese bond market adds another layer of complexity to BOJ decisions. Rising yields have begun to attract some foreign capital back to JGBs, but higher rates also raise the government’s financing costs. A September hike could help stabilise the yen but would also push up borrowing costs for the government and corporations, testing Japan’s massive debt load and bond‑market stability.

Overall, the latest survey shows market expectations have shifted from “whether the BOJ will keep raising rates” to “how fast the hikes will come and how high the final rate will be.” Amid yen weakness, import‑driven inflation, Middle‑East energy shocks and fiscal‑expansion worries, the September BOJ meeting could become a pivotal turning point for the next tightening cycle. If the BOJ lifts rates to 1.25% as markets expect, it would further accelerate Japan’s rate‑normalisation path and could pave the way for rates of 1.5% or even 1.75%+ by around 2027.

items.title_en: NY Forex: Dollar Weakens as Bond Market Rebounds, Market Awaits PCE and Jackson Hole
paras: 美元周二(26日)走弱，市場風險情緒受到油價與美國公債殖利率下滑的帶動而升溫。同時，加拿大幣在前一個交易日走跌後小幅反彈，加拿大政府以報復性關稅反制華盛頓的措施。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.1%，報98.93。目前徘徊在5月中旬以來最低水準附近。
固定收益市場持續受到外匯市場參與者的關注，美國公債殖利率連續第二個交易日走低。一項關鍵推動因素是CNBC周一的一則報導，稱華盛頓可能動用規模近1兆美元的財政部一般帳戶(TGA)，協助為上周宣布增加的長天期公債回購提供資金。市場將這項措施視為一項出乎意料的干預行動，目的是抑制殖利率上升，尤其是長天期殖利率。
經濟學家與分析師普遍認為，美國財政部的干預只是針對更大問題所採取的不可持續短期解決方案，而這個更大的問題受到華盛頓財政債務不斷膨脹所引發的市場擔憂所推動。上周，美國政府債務突破40兆美元，導致財政部宣布措施後所帶來的全部漲幅遭到逆轉。
一般而言，公債殖利率上升會產生類似升息的效果，因為這會推高消費者與企業的借貸成本，通常有利於美元走強。然而，上周美國債務的消息引發了市場對美國財政狀況的疑慮，而在這種環境下，投資人傾向將資金從法定貨幣轉向黃金或加密貨幣等硬資產。
事實上，美元指數上周下跌近1%，黃金與加密貨幣均上漲。
Macquarie全球外匯與利率策略師Thierry Wizman表示，「美元昨天收復了上周跌幅的一小部分，但我們認為，市場更重要的變化，是美國長天期公債殖利率自上周中旬觸及高點後持續下降。」
他表示，「也許有些交易員注意到了自昨天開始出現的報導(或外洩消息)，稱美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)可能會動用財政部一般帳戶，以擴大長天期公債的回購規模。視干預規模而定，這將是另一項試圖管理長天期公債淨供給的措施，這些債券會發行至高評級長天期債券市場。」
Wizman補充，「任何旨在單純透過降低市場流通中的美國政府債務平均剩餘期限來『扭轉』美國殖利率曲線的操作，本身並不一定代表貨幣政策具『刺激性』，也不會單獨創造刺激性的財政效果。它也沒有直接處理赤字『問題』。但債務管理政策仍可能非常有用，具體取決於干預的規模，而非其對殖利率的影響。」
目前利率市場目前關注焦點已轉向周三公布的7月核心個人消費支出(PCE)物價指數數據，該指標被廣泛視為聯準會(Fed)偏好的通膨衡量指標。之後市場焦點將轉向聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)周五在傑克森霍爾(Jackson Hole)年度會議上的主題演講。
加拿大出手反擊 加幣反彈
其他主要貨幣方面，加拿大幣兌美元走強，美元兌加幣下跌0.1%，至1.3827加幣。
加幣前一個交易日走弱，因華盛頓與渥太華為達成貿易協議所進行的談判破裂，而新的50%美國關稅於周六開始生效，適用於價值276億美元的加拿大進口商品。
加拿大周二表示，自9月8日起，將「對美國根據第338條款與第232條款關稅所針對的產品徵收15%、25%及50%的報復性關稅，各項產品的稅率將與美國相應的稅率一致。」
根據加拿大政府的聲明，這些關稅將適用於價值276億美元的美國進口商品，涵蓋鋼鐵、乳製品、家電、農業設備、紙漿與紙張，以及電子產品等產業。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.1%，至1.3650美元，受到英國公債殖利率保持韌性及服務業價格走勢強勁的支撐。
歐元兌美元小幅上漲0.1%，至1.1674美元，在區域交易員消化德國經濟成長優於預期的數據後，延續近期漲勢。德國國內生產毛額(GDP)年增率達1.0%，高於市場預期。
日元兌美元持平，美元兌日元匯率維持在159.10不變。
澳幣兌美元上漲0.2%，至0.7164美元。澳洲央行8月會議紀要顯示，政策制定者對核心物價居高不下是否足以支持再次升息仍存在分歧。

paras_en: The dollar weakened on Tuesday (the 26th) as risk sentiment was lifted by falling oil prices and a drop in U.S. Treasury yields. At the same time, the Canadian dollar, after falling the previous trading day, made a modest rebound as Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs in response to Washington's measures.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, fell 0.1% to 98.93, hovering near its lowest level since mid‑May.

The fixed‑income market continues to draw attention from forex participants, with U.S. Treasury yields slipping for the second consecutive session. A key driver was a CNBC report on Monday that Washington might tap the Treasury’s General Account (TGA), roughly $1 trillion, to fund the expanded long‑term Treasury repurchase announced last week. Markets saw this as an unexpected intervention aimed at curbing rising yields, especially at the long end.

Economists and analysts generally view the Treasury’s move as an unsustainable short‑term fix to a larger problem driven by concerns over Washington’s ever‑growing fiscal debt. Last week U.S. government debt topped $40 trillion, causing the gains from the Treasury’s announcement to be quickly erased.

Normally, higher bond yields act like a rate hike, raising borrowing costs for consumers and firms and typically supporting a stronger dollar. However, last week’s debt news sparked doubts about U.S. fiscal health, prompting investors to shift money from fiat currencies into hard assets such as gold and cryptocurrencies.
In fact, the dollar index fell nearly 1% last week, while gold and crypto both rose.

Macquarie global FX and rates strategist Thierry Wizman said, “The dollar reclaimed a small portion of last week’s losses yesterday, but the more important market shift is the continued decline in long‑term U.S. Treasury yields since they peaked in mid‑week.”

He added, “Some traders may have noticed reports (or leaks) starting yesterday that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could draw on the General Account to expand the scale of long‑term Treasury repurchases. Depending on the size of the intervention, this would be another attempt to manage the net supply of long‑dated bonds issued to the high‑grade market.”

Wizman further noted, “Any operation that simply tries to ‘flatten’ the U.S. yield curve by shortening the average remaining maturity of debt in circulation does not necessarily represent a ‘stimulative’ monetary policy, nor does it create a standalone fiscal stimulus. It also does not directly address the deficit ‘problem.’ However, debt‑management policy can still be very useful, depending on the scale of the intervention rather than its immediate impact on yields.”

The focus in the rates market has now shifted to the July core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index due on Wednesday, a metric widely regarded as the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. After that, attention will turn to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s keynote speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference on Friday.
Canada strikes back – the loonie rebounds
Among other major currencies, the Canadian dollar strengthened against the U.S. dollar, with USD/CAD down 0.1% to 1.3827 CAD.

The loonie had weakened the previous session after negotiations between Washington and Ottawa over a trade deal collapsed, and a new 50% U.S. tariff took effect on Saturday covering $27.6 billion of Canadian imports.

Canada said on Tuesday that, starting September 8, it will impose retaliatory tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on U.S. products subject to tariffs under sections 338 and 232, matching the corresponding U.S. rates for each product category.

According to the Canadian statement, the tariffs will apply to $27.6 billion of U.S. imports, covering steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, among other sectors.
The British pound rose 0.1% against the dollar to $1.3650, supported by resilient UK gilt yields and strong services‑price trends.
The euro edged up 0.1% to $1.1674 as regional traders digested Germany’s better‑than‑expected growth data, extending the recent rally. German GDP grew 1.0% year‑on‑year, above forecasts.
The yen was flat against the dollar, with USD/JPY unchanged at 159.10.
The Australian dollar gained 0.2% to $0.7164. Minutes from the RBA’s August meeting showed policymakers remain divided on whether persistently high core inflation justifies another rate hike.
